content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Environment Management and Secret Handling in Postman"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When testing APIs across multiple stages such as Development, Staging, and Production, hardcoding URLs, tokens, and credentials becomes unmaintainable and insecure. Postman solves this challenge through Environments and Secret Handling."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Environments and Variables"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"An environment in Postman is a set of key-value pairs that lets you switch context without modifying your request URLs or bodies. Variables can be scoped at different levels, including Global, Environment, Collection, and Local."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Environment Variables: Specific to a selected environment (e.g., base_url for staging)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Collection Variables: Available to all requests inside a specific collection, regardless of the active environment."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global Variables: Accessible across all collections and environments within your workspace."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step-by-Step: Creating an Environment"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open Postman and click on the 'Environments' quick look icon (eye symbol) in the top-right corner."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Add' to create a new environment and name it 'Development'."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Add a variable named 'base_url' and set its initial and current value to 'https://api-dev.example.com'."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Save' to store your environment."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Variables in Requests"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once defined, you can reference variables in your request URLs, headers, and body using double curly braces syntax."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"GET {{base_url}}/users/profile"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Secret Handling Best Practices"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Managing sensitive data like API keys, passwords, and OAuth tokens requires caution, especially when collaborating via Postman Cloud or exporting collections to source control."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the 'Secret' variable type introduced by Postman to mask sensitive values automatically in the UI."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Never commit 'Current Values' containing production secrets to public Git repositories."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage Postman scripts to dynamically capture tokens into environment variables instead of hardcoding them."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Capturing Tokens via Test Scripts"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can automatically extract an authentication token from a login response and save it to an environment variable for subsequent requests."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"var jsonData = pm.response.json();\npm.environment.set(\"auth_token\", jsonData.token);"}]
